diagnosis: The incumbent is massively over-jammed rather than merely under-polished: the plot shows hundreds of pairs tied at the maximum to within $10^{-16}$, contact degrees of roughly 22--43 per point against only 21 tangential degrees of freedom per point, and zero rattlers. Consequently the LP/gradient feasible cone is essentially empty, explaining why LP polishing gained only $2.7\times10^{-7}$, while small kicks return to the same contact graph and large kicks destroy dozens of contacts simultaneously and quench to worse minima; repeated large LPs then cause the 200s timeouts. The missing structural property is a different, more balanced contact topology---some slack or rattler-like mobility and more uniform degree/stress---that permits a collective rearrangement, not another local squeeze of this graph.
